title: The Good Shepherd
blurb: Follow the shepherd image from the prophets and the Psalms to the Gospels, where Christ names himself the Good Shepherd and commissions Peter to feed his sheep.

steps.title: Shepherds who fail, a God who rescues
steps.intro: Through Ezekiel, God rebukes Israel's leaders for feeding themselves rather than the flock. He then promises to search for the scattered sheep himself, setting the pattern for the shepherd imagery that follows in the Psalms and the Gospels.

quote.text: By the Prophet Ezekiel the Lord rebukes the shepherds, and among other things says of the sheep, “The wandering sheep have ye not recalled.”

steps.question: Who has looked for you when you were scattered, and whom might you be called to seek out?

steps.title: The Lord is my shepherd
steps.intro: David's best-loved psalm speaks of pasture, quiet waters, a darkened valley, a table and a house of the Lord. Christians have long prayed it as the voice of one who trusts the shepherd completely, in both peaceful and fearful seasons.

quote.text: He hath brought me forth in the narrow ways, wherein few walk, of His righteousness; not for my merit’s sake, but for His Name’s sake.

steps.question: Which line of this psalm do you most need to pray this week, and why?

steps.title: He will gather the lambs
steps.intro: After the announcement of good news to Jerusalem, Isaiah pictures the Lord coming with strength and also gathering lambs in his arms. Gentleness and power meet in the same shepherd.

quote.text: And that He also calls us lambs, the Spirit by the mouth of Isaiah is an unimpeachable witness: “He will feed His flock like a shepherd, He will gather the lambs with His arm,”

steps.question: Where do you see strength and tenderness held together, and what does that teach you about God?

steps.title: Leaving the ninety-nine
steps.intro: Jesus answers criticism of his table fellowship with the parable of a shepherd who goes after one lost sheep. He carries it home and calls his neighbours to rejoice, so that heaven's joy over a repentant sinner becomes the point of the story.

quote.text: I have read in the Gospel that the Good Shepherd leaves the faithful ones of His flock in the desert to hasten after the lost sheep.

steps.question: When have you been the lost sheep, and who or what carried you back?

steps.title: The door and the voice
steps.intro: Jesus speaks of a sheepfold, a gatekeeper and a shepherd whose voice the sheep know. He calls himself the door of the sheep, the way in to safety, pasture and life in abundance.

quote.text: For many indeed in the Church are following after earthly profit, and yet preach Christ, and through them is heard the voice of Christ; and the sheep follow, not the hireling, but the Shepherd’s voice speaking through the hireling.

steps.question: What voices compete for your attention, and how do you learn to recognise the shepherd's voice?

steps.title: The shepherd lays down his life
steps.intro: Jesus declares himself the good shepherd and contrasts him with a hired hand who flees. He says he lays down his life freely and has other sheep, so that there will be one flock and one shepherd.

quote.text: You are the Good Shepherd who, to fulfill Your obedience, laid down His life for Your lambs, and made for us a bath of His Blood.

steps.question: What does it mean to you that the shepherd's care is described as freely given and costly?

steps.title: Feed my sheep
steps.intro: After the resurrection Jesus asks Peter three times, 'Do you love me?' and each time entrusts him with the care of his lambs and sheep. The shepherd shares his own pastoral charge with a forgiven disciple.

quote.text: If, then, the care of feeding is the proof of loving, whosoever abounds in virtues, and yet refuses to feed the flock of God, is convicted of not loving the chief Shepherd.

steps.question: Whom has Christ placed in your care, and how can you feed or serve them this week?
